title: Welcome to Bedrock
body:
# Your notes. Solid ground.

Welcome to **Bedrock**. A quiet place to collect ideas, make connections, and build something that lasts.

## Start with one good thought

Write a note. Give it a clear name. Then use `[[Note title]]` to connect it to another idea.

- **Write** to work in Markdown.
- **Read** for a clean page.
- **Both** to keep source and preview together.

## Find the layers

Open [[Linked thinking]] to follow a connection, or choose **Atlas** to see the whole notebook. The **Links** panel holds backlinks and your outline when you need them.

> Build a useful notebook one thought at a time.

## A place to begin

- [ ] Capture an idea in [[Quick ideas]]
- [ ] Make a plan in [[Project notebook]]
- [ ] Start a daily note

Your notes are stored in SQLite on your own server. Open **Settings** for imports, exports, backups, and your server connection.

#start-here #notes

title: Linked thinking
body:
# Think in connections

A note is a small unit of thought. A link gives that thought a place in a bigger picture.

When you write [[Your knowledge garden]], Bedrock records an outgoing link. That note then shows this one as a **backlink**.

## A useful habit

Before you finish a note, ask: *what does this remind me of?*

Try connecting your [[Reading list]] to a project in [[Project notebook]].

#thinking #connections

title: Your knowledge garden
body:
# Grow a knowledge garden

Collect seeds in [[Quick ideas]]. Let useful notes grow. Connect them with [[Linked thinking]].

## Follow the threads

The graph is a map of internal links. Click a point to open its note. Drag points to arrange the view.

A garden gets better with care. Return to your [[Reading list]], remove what no longer serves you, and make room for new ideas.

#thinking #notes

title: Quick ideas
body:
# Leave a little room for curiosity

## Things to explore

- A notebook that makes connections visible
- Small tools that work without an account
- The relationship between [[Daily practice]] and creative work

An idea doesn't need to be finished to be worth keeping. Move a promising one into [[Project notebook]].

title: Reading list
body:
# Read. Reflect. Connect.

## On the shelf

- [ ] A book about systems thinking
- [ ] An essay about learning in public
- [x] A guide to Markdown

## Reading notes

Don't just summarize. Write what changed your mind, then connect it to [[Linked thinking]] or a question in [[Quick ideas]].

title: Project notebook
body:
# Build something small

**Goal:** turn one useful idea into something you can use.

## Next steps

- [ ] Pick an idea from [[Quick ideas]]
- [ ] Describe the smallest useful version
- [ ] Make a little progress with [[Daily practice]]

## Keep it simple

Start with the part that matters most. Make it work. Then make it pleasant.

title: Daily practice
body:
# Small steps, taken often

A place to pause, reflect, and start again. Use the calendar icon to create today's daily note.

## Three questions

1. What did I notice today?
2. What am I learning?
3. What is one next step for [[Project notebook]]?

A useful ritual connects [[Quick ideas]] with action.

#daily #thinking
